# Gradify

> Gradify turns your notes into flashcards and mind maps checked against what you wrote, and schedules revision with spaced repetition (FSRS) up to your exam. Upload a PDF or paste notes in Notes Studio with no account; every card links to the line in your notes it came from, and cards that don't fully match are marked "to check". Free, with free courses in 30+ subjects from GCSE to postgraduate.

Gradify is free to use (no card). Gradify Pro (£10 a month) adds planning and removes limits. Specialist sites live in folders of getgradify.com, one account across all of them.

## Product
- [Gradify app and Notes Studio](https://getgradify.com/app.html): upload notes (PDF, text) and get checked flashcards, mind maps and a revision plan
- [PDF to flashcards](https://getgradify.com/pdf-to-flashcards/): turn a lecture PDF into source-checked flashcards
- [Lecture notes to mind map](https://getgradify.com/lecture-notes-to-mind-map/): an editable mind map from notes
- [Notes to cheat sheet](https://getgradify.com/notes-to-cheat-sheet/): a one-page revision sheet or key-terms sheet
- [Pricing](https://getgradify.com/pricing.html): Free, Gradify Pro and Gradify Ultra
- [Quality and coverage](https://getgradify.com/quality.html): how lessons are audited and which qualifications are covered
- [About Gradify](https://getgradify.com/about.html): who builds it and how content is checked

## Free tools
- [UK degree classification calculator](https://getgradify.com/tools/degree-classification-calculator/): Work out a 1st, 2:1, 2:2 or 3rd from your module marks.
- [Final exam grade calculator](https://getgradify.com/tools/final-grade-calculator/): The mark you need on the final to hit your target.
- [Weighted grade calculator](https://getgradify.com/tools/weighted-grade-calculator/): Your module average from assessments of different weights.
- [GPA calculator (4.0 scale)](https://getgradify.com/tools/gpa-calculator/): Your grade point average from letter grades and credits.
- [Exam countdown and revision hours](https://getgradify.com/tools/exam-countdown/): Days to go, real study hours left, and a story card to share.
- [Spaced repetition schedule generator](https://getgradify.com/tools/spaced-repetition-schedule/): Review dates for any topic, as a calendar file.

## Guides
- [The complete guide to active recall for exams](https://getgradify.com/guides/active-recall/): Active recall means testing yourself by pulling information out of memory, instead of reading it again
- [Active recall vs re-reading: which actually works?](https://getgradify.com/guides/active-recall-vs-rereading/): Active recall works better
- [How to use active recall for science subjects](https://getgradify.com/guides/active-recall-for-science/): In science, use flashcards for definitions and facts, draw processes and diagrams from memory on a blank page, and practise calculations as unseen problems
- [The best active recall schedule before finals](https://getgradify.com/guides/active-recall-schedule-before-finals/): Spend the first four weeks covering every topic with active recall and spaced reviews, then use the last two weeks for timed past papers and your weakest topics
- [How to make good flashcards: 9 rules](https://getgradify.com/guides/how-to-make-good-flashcards/): Good flashcards test one idea each, ask a precise question with one right answer, and come from your own course material
- [How to revise in two weeks](https://getgradify.com/guides/how-to-revise-in-two-weeks/): Triage first: list every topic, rank them by how likely they are to come up and how weak you are, and cut what you can't cover
- [The 7 best study tools for university students in 2026](https://getgradify.com/guides/best-study-tools-for-university-students/): Anki is best for serious long-term memorisation, Quizlet for quick shared vocabulary sets, Notion for organising a whole degree, and Gradify for turning your own lecture notes into checked flashcards and a revision plan
